lead.headline: RBI clamps down on dollar demand to defend the rupee, and will sell dollars straight to the three state oil companies
lead.short: Firms buying foreign currency forwards worth more than $2 million to cover imports will have to lodge 20% of the value in cash with the RBI through their bank. Cancelled rupee derivative contracts can no longer be rebooked, and the limit for hedging without proof of an underlying exposure falls from $100 million to $5 million. From Monday the RBI will meet the entire daily dollar needs of Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL itself, keeping their purchases out of the market.
more: The measures came on a Saturday after the rupee fell close to its record low, with oil above $100 and foreign investors selling Indian shares for days.

why.text: A defence this heavy says the RBI sees real pressure on the rupee; for a household it means imported things, foreign travel and overseas fees stay costly.

seconds.headline: Police detain more than 1,600 in Delhi to stop the protest against the Election Commission, including its leaders on their plane
seconds.byline: TIMES OF INDIA · SCROLL · NDTV · 10 OCT
seconds.short: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convenor Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were taken off their Mumbai flight on landing; Dhruv Rathee was held at his Gurugram home. More than 400 student marchers, lawyers walking from the Supreme Court, CPI(M) leaders at Jantar Mantar and two Scroll journalists covering the protest were also detained. The Chief Justice intervened to get the lawyers released.

why.text: The biggest preventive detention in the capital in years, over a protest about who runs elections.

update.new: The protest day began with mass detentions, including the organisers on their plane.
update.front: Mass detentions in the capital on the day of the protest are front-page news on their own.

facts.leaders: Dipke, Das, Ranka held on plane

seconds.headline: India make 249 in Ranchi and still lose: Shai Hope's 102 from 45 balls powers West Indies' record chase
seconds.short: West Indies reached 252 for 4 with nine balls to spare, their highest successful chase and the second-highest in all T20 internationals. Hope hit nine sixes and Sherfane Rutherford made 84 from 37. The series is 1–1 with the third match in Indore on Sunday.

why.text: A 249 that was not enough exposes India's bowling, which Gambhir says is now playing for careers.

update.new: West Indies won the second T20I by six wickets; the series is level.
update.front: India losing after making 249 is the cricket news of the week.

seconds.headline: Navi Pillay, the judge who defended Mandela and led the UN's Gaza inquiry, wins the Nobel Peace Prize
seconds.short: The committee said the South African, now a judge at the International Court of Justice and once UN human rights chief, had shown "that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence". The UN commission she chaired concluded last year that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Trump, nominated again by Pakistan's prime minister hours before, said Norway had an "indelible stain".

why.text: A prize for international law in a year when the US has sanctioned the International Criminal Court.

screen.title: Drishyam: The Conclusion
screen.reason: A satisfying close to the franchise: Devgn's silent Vijay and Jaideep Ahlawat's cop carry it, though critics differ on how much the slow first half and the courtroom twists cost it.

screen.title: Verity
screen.reason: Most critics found the Colleen Hoover thriller silly and unconvincing, wasting Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson; a few enjoyed it as knowing camp.

screen.title: Resident Evil
screen.reason: Zach Cregger's reboot is gory, fast and often funny, with Austin Abrams a likeable lead; its critics say the chaos outruns any real dread.

screen.title: Heart of the Beast
screen.reason: An old-fashioned man-and-dog survival story in Alaska, lifted by Brad Pitt and the dog; reviews run from deeply moving to serviceable.

screen.title: The Uprising
screen.reason: Andrew Garfield is committed and the battle scenes hit hard, but most critics found Paul Greengrass's Peasants' Revolt epic thin, grim and flat.
